To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the minimizing point of an empirically centered df converges to the unique minimizing point of the time-transformed homogeneous (with drift) Poisson process.
the minimizing point of Fn - F 0 converges in distribution to a random variable which is a time-transformation of an almost sure unique minimizing Poisson-process.

the minimizing point is the unique solution of a functional equation and that this solution is the unique minimizer of a time-transformed homogeneous two-sided Poisson-process with drift, where the time-transformation and drift are of the form |t| α.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a generalization of the classical Glivenko-Cantelli-theorem.
a nonregular problem of empirical process theory.

the limit distribution of the minimizing point of an empirical process in nonregular experiments, where the limit distribution has an interesting interpretation as a two-sided time-transformation of a homogeneous Poisson-process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in nonregular experiments, the minimizing point of Fn - F0 converges in distribution to an almost sure unique point, which is the almost sure minimizing point of a homogeneous Poisson process with drift.
the minimizing point of an incorrectly centered empirical process is a time-transformed Poisson-process with drift.
the limiting distribution is the same as the one for the correctly centered empirical process in regular experiments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we show that in the case of nonregular experiments ( F ≠ F 0 ) the minimizer is asymptotically equivalent to the minimizer of the centered empirical process, but it is not a minimizer of the empirical process.
the minimizing point of a non-centered empirical df has the same distribution as the minimizing point of an empirical df which is centered at the unique point of discontinuity of F.
in a nonregular experiment the minimization of the empirical process is a powerful tool to estimate the point τ.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the limit distribution of the minimizer is independent of the local smoothness order α.
the minimizer of the empirical df is a nonregular estimator.
the minimization of the empirical process is a robust tool to estimate the point τ of local regularity of the underlying df.
